why: To raise both feature counts by one you either buy a '11' model or buy one '01' plus one '10' model; '00' models never help and a lone single-feature model is wasted. So build a list of 'units' (each '11' cost, and the i-th cheapest A-only paired with the i-th cheapest B-only), sort it, and the answer for k is the sum of the k cheapest units, a prefix sum over a sorted list.
hints: Classify models into '11', A-only, B-only and useless '00'. What is the cheapest way to add +1 to both counts?
Either one '11' model or a pair (A-only, B-only). Pair the cheapest A-only with the cheapest B-only, the second with the second, and so on.
Put all '11' costs and all pair costs into one list, sort it, and take running sums: answer[k-1] = sum of the k smallest units, -1 once units run out. O(n log n).
pitfalls: Check the character order: '01' means feature A only and '10' means B only (per the statement), but only the pairing structure matters.
Pairs must use the cheapest remaining singles on each side; sorting each side and zipping guarantees that.
Entries beyond the number of available units are -1.
